rationale:
Evidence: the best raced design is iteration 7 (score 58.17; oval 63.49, s-bend 66.85, slalom 44.19; no completions). Every run ended off_track, with progress 0.11 to 0.16. Iteration 6 (sensor row y 0.06) scored 57.80, so the y 0.08 change added 0.38. That gain is small, but it is the best measured result.

Critique handling. I reject the round-2 revision's base_speed 1.3. The critique's arithmetic holds: the score is progress times the line-loss and rms factors, so any progress lost to slower driving is lost directly. Lower speed also has no measured link to fewer line-loss events, and the revision's own reversal rule anticipates a score drop. Its speed mechanism is also unconfirmed: no measured link exists between base_speed and the early exit. I accept the critique's points that the targets are partly unachievable at baseline (slalom progress 0.1075 against a 0.16 target; oval steering_oscillation already above 0.16) and that the exit is early and unexplained. I do not add a second change this iteration, because I have no single change with a credible mechanism and a non-negative expected score.

What I kept: the exact raced iteration 7 design, which the round-2 revision also used as its baseline. What I changed: nothing relative to that baseline. I restore base_speed 1.5, which reverses the round-2 revision's speed change.

Expected result: about 58.17 again, since the seeds are fixed. A result above 58.17 would support keeping y 0.08. A result below it would point to the speed or sensor change being harmful, and I would then revert y to 0.06. The open risk is the early oval and slalom start transient, which only per-step telemetry can locate.
